current.text: LaMelo Ball was traded from Charlotte to Minnesota.
He is one of Minnesota's four set starters, with Edwards, McDaniels and Gobert. The fifth starting spot is open.
He is expected to run the offense, handle the ball much more than Edwards and lead the team in assists.
Experts expect his minutes to rise to 30 to 32 a night in Minnesota.
Experts expect his usage to drop to about 28% next to Edwards. His assist rate may still rise, and one expert projects his overall production to go up by about 7%.
Minnesota is expected to compete, so he should not be held out for tanking reasons.
Experts see value at his market rank of about 22 to 24, even after an injury discount. One expert values him in the mid-30s USD and paid 30 USD in a mock auction.
He is a tier 3 point guard. If you expect only 28 minutes or about 50 games, move him to tier 4.
The new team and the ankle risk are named as concerns for this season.
Minnesota has a two-game week in the matchup starting March 15, which is our playoff week 20.
Because of the two-game playoff week, move him slightly down your board and pass on him in close calls.
Back-to-back rest is not a real worry for him.

durable.text: He is one of the best passers and transition players in the NBA, and one expert calls him an elite offensive player who is underrated.
In Charlotte he played with a usage rate of about 30% and a high assist rate.
He takes a very high share of his shots from three and has unlimited range.
Finishing at the rim is his biggest weakness, and he does not get to the free throw line much.
He helps a lot in assists and threes but drags down FG% on high volume.
He commits many turnovers, which hurts the TO category.
He adds rebounds on top of assists and points, which most assist guards do not.
He has a long history of ankle injuries, including impingement. He has also played 70 or more games twice.
Experts disagree on his health risk. One calls health the biggest question about him. Others say the ankle fears are overblown because many of his missed games came from Charlotte tanking.

note: LaMelo Ball is a strong threes and assists source who costs you in FG% and turnovers. He fits best on punt FG% and punt TO teams. Prices are close together: Yahoo has him at 31 USD (average cost 30.2), ESPN at 36 USD (27.2), and he went for 29 USD in our league last year. Experts value him in the mid-30s, so 30 to 33 USD is fair, but the two-game playoff week starting March 15 (our week 20) is a reason not to stretch. Early in the season, check that his minutes really reach 30 or more, how his assists hold up next to Edwards, and how his ankles are doing.
